entities.name: Aryl nitro reduction
observations: The reactant nitroarene is converted to the corresponding primary aniline while retaining aryl chloride and aryl bromide substituents.
Closest exact precedent uses iron in ethanol at 100 °C for 1 hour and reports 98% yield.
Recorded reaction mixture/workup includes acetic acid, water, sodium bicarbonate, and sodium acetate.

entities.name: Fe/EtOH nitro reduction
observations: Iron powder in ethanol at approximately 80–100 °C is a plausible chemoselective condition for reducing the aromatic nitro group to an aniline.
The exact precedent used Fe/EtOH at 100 °C for 1 hour with 98% yield; aqueous/acetic-acid components and bicarbonate/acetate appear in the record.

entities.name: Aryl nitroarene substrate
observations: Substrate contains an aromatic nitro group together with aryl chloride and aryl bromide substituents.

entities.name: Aryl aniline product
observations: Product is the corresponding aromatic primary amine; aryl chloride and aryl bromide are retained.
